ambiguities.impact: Read literally as a space of pointwise functions, ||X||_Lp can vanish on a nonzero function supported on a null set and is only a seminorm. The norm and Banach claims therefore require the standard implicit Lp convention of almost-sure equivalence classes (or an equivalent identification).

contract_plain_english: Fix a probability space. For every exponent p from 1 through infinity, including p = infinity, form the classical real Lp space of random variables with finite Lp quantity. For finite p this quantity is (E|X|^p)^(1/p), and at p = infinity it is ess sup |X|. The source separately asserts (1) that this quantity is a norm and (2) that the resulting space is complete, hence Banach. It cites Minkowski's inequality (1.4); the nearby text presents Minkowski as the triangle inequality and explicitly derives the norm property, but it gives no separate completeness proof. The standard almost-sure quotient convention is necessary for a true norm even though that convention is left implicit in the passage.
